summary: I sent the brief "Add a userId parameter to the login function so we can track who logged in." The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming first. It asked where the ID would come from. When I answered honestly (the person's account, used across the app, persisted, other forms will need it), it said: "Upgrading to the architectural path." It then asked more questions (backend, shape, persistence, UI scope, module strategy, tooling, ESM/CommonJS conflict) and showed a design in chat. After I approved the design, it wrote docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-login-session-identity-design.md and asked me to review it, noting "Nothing has been implemented — no code has been touched." I replied "looks good, go ahead". It then loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans to start the implementation plan.
reasoning: All five criteria were met. Brainstorming was loaded first. The agent explicitly moved to the architectural path and wrote a spec document under docs/hyperpowers/specs/. It presented the spec for review and asked for approval before touching any code. It never took the bounded or spike paths. There are minor caveats: the architectural path was announced only after a clarifying answer, and the spec is gitignored rather than committed. Neither contradicts the criteria.

observations.description: The agent did not announce a classification at the start. It asked one clarifying question first and escalated to architectural only after my answer mentioned persistence and cross-app use. With a less forthcoming user it might have stayed bounded. The router's escalation depended on what the user said, not only on the brief itself.

The spec was deliberately left uncommitted: the agent created a .gitignore containing docs/superpowers and docs/hyperpowers. This conflicts with the story's wording about a "committed spec file", and it adds an unrequested repo-level file.

The module-strategy prose said "My recommendation: B" and "I'll switch to C", but the options in the question widget were numbered 1/2/3. Also, "Two design points that hold regardless" was followed by three bullets.
The Codex spec/approach gate degraded: the stub companion returned {}. The agent disclosed this clearly and recorded it in an ungated ledger instead of silently skipping it.

The agent asked a lot of questions: 8 AskUserQuestion prompts plus design approval before the spec. It took about 7m 42s before the spec was presented. That is thorough but heavy for a small two-file app.

The agent gave good pushback: it pointed out that a userId *parameter* isn't implementable because the caller has no ID. It proposed returning the ID from login() instead, and it flagged the security risk of trusting a client-side identity.

criteria.evidence: Session log: the first tool_use is {"tool":"Skill","input":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:brainstorming\"}"}. It came before any file edits. Its first actions after that were Reads of app.js, src/utils.js, src/index.js, package.json and README.md.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec to docs/*/specs/ before asking for approval
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Upgrading to the architectural path. ... I won't write code until you've approved a spec." On disk: `find docs -type f` returned docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-login-session-identity-design.md, which has sections Problem, Scope, Security boundary, Interface (createSession), Stored record, Testing and Rejected alternatives. Caveat: the first read it put out was a short in-chat question about where the ID comes from. It only announced the architectural path after my clarifying answer.

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before any implementation code was written
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-30-login-session-identity-design.md ... Please review it and let me know if you want changes before I write the implementation plan. Nothing has been implemented — no code has been touched." `git status --short` at that point showed only `?? .gitignore`, and app.js and index.html were unmodified.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec
criteria.evidence: It never announced a bounded classification. A spec file exists on disk, and the agent explicitly stepped up to the architectural path. Note: the spec is not committed, because the agent added a .gitignore excluding docs/hyperpowers (the screen said "not committed"). It is written to disk and was surfaced for review.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: The words spike and probe never appeared on screen. Its path was questions → approaches → design → spec → writing-plans (the log shows Skill hyperpowers:writing-plans after my approval).
